correctness.rationale: The diagonal Gamma integral gives q^(n+1); averaging any bounded symbol yields a bounded radial symbol. Its Laplace transform is holomorphic on Re z>0, while its moment generating function is a rational expression with simple poles at distinct -alpha(u^k-1); therefore every forbidden coefficient vanishes. Allowed coefficients yield an explicit bounded symbol with the right moments. Hermite-polynomial density proves uniqueness. Equidistribution and finite root-of-unity counts prove the density law. The boundary Re(u^k)=1 is explicitly included, and k=0 and t>0 are treated.

value.rationale: The single bounded-symbol Toeplitz class is not multiplicatively closed even within the polynomial algebra generated by one natural compact unimodular phase Toeplitz operator. The theorem completely describes which finite polynomial combinations survive, proves there is no cancellation between forbidden powers, and quantifies infinitely many such successes through a sharp phase-arithmetic density that jumps at rational resonances. This addresses the natural, explicitly distinguished gap between membership in the generated Toeplitz algebra and exact bounded-symbol representability; the computation is not an arbitrary finite slice.
